title: The Moth Finds the Porch Light

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Choose one comfortable breath sensation as your porch light: nostrils, chest, or belly.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Feel one inhale and one exhale. Let attention rest near the small warm signal.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [faint night breeze rustling] Imagine the mind as a moth circling through the dark. Wandering is what minds do.
[soft, slow, warm voice] When you notice thought, sound, or feeling has carried attention away, name it lightly and return to the porch light.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] The return is the practice. No flight path needs to be erased.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Stay with three breaths: one... two... three... feeling each from beginning to end.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release counting and notice the most vivid detail of breathing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] If restlessness appears, feel it for one moment, then return without argument.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Again and again, the moth discovers the light. Each discovery is new.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Rest with fewer words now: breathing... wandering... noticing... home.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Widen attention to include the whole body and room.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes. Let attention fly freely, remembering that it knows a way back.
